revision_note: Rewritten in review round 2. The round-1 receipt described a false isolation hazard (see corrected_incident_from_round_1 below) and, because of that false hazard, never actually ran the rename/delete correctness check. This revision corrects the record, cleans up the round-1 side effects, and runs the check.

corrected_incident_from_round_1.round_1_claim: Starting a standalone `serena start-mcp-server --project <disposable-repo> --transport streamable-http` process mutated the shared, host-wide ~/.serena/serena_config.yml (used by every concurrently running Serena instance on this host), and this could not be fully reverted because no pre-migration backup existed.
corrected_incident_from_round_1.why_false: The live Serena MCP servers on this host (the ones backing this and other concurrent sessions) run with the environment variable SERENA_HOME=/home/example/.local/share/codex-ecosystem/context/serena-home, confirmed via /proc/<pid>/environ for multiple running `serena start-mcp-server --project-from-cwd` processes. That directory has its own serena_config.yml (mtime 2026-09-22 19:43, before the round-1 run) which still lists its own registered projects and was never touched by the round-1 run. ~/.serena/serena_config.yml did not exist before round 1: Serena's own log for that run says 'Serena configuration file not found at /home/example/.serena/serena_config.yml, autogenerating...' followed by 'Legacy configuration was migrated; re-saving configuration file' (the newly generated template being re-saved, not an edit to a pre-existing file). So (a) no live/shared Serena instance reads ~/.serena/serena_config.yml, and (b) there was no pre-existing file to fail to revert -- the whole ~/.serena/serena_config.yml plus the language_servers/, logs/, and prompt_templates/ directories under ~/.serena were newly created by the round-1 run and were therefore fully revertible by deletion, which is what round 2 did.
corrected_incident_from_round_1.correct_fix_for_isolation: Set SERENA_HOME to a directory under the unit's own cache path (/home/example/.cache/gap-wave2-20260923/code-navigation/) before invoking any serena command or starting any serena process, so no global state under the real ~/.serena is touched at all, rather than trying to snapshot/restore ~/.serena/serena_config.yml.
corrected_incident_from_round_1.cleanup_performed: Backed up (to /home/example/.cache/gap-wave2-20260923/code-navigation/cleanup-backup/) then deleted ~/.serena/language_servers/, ~/.serena/logs/, ~/.serena/prompt_templates/, and ~/.serena/serena_config.yml -- all four were created at 2026-09-22 20:39:09-20:39:52 by the round-1 run (confirmed via `ls -la --time-style=full-iso ~/.serena/`); only ~/.serena/memories/ (present since 2026-09-20) predates the run and was left untouched. After cleanup, ~/.serena/ contains only memories/, i.e. its pre-round-1 state.

preregistration.expectation: With SERENA_HOME pointed at an isolated directory under /home/example/.cache/gap-wave2-20260923/code-navigation/ (never the real ~/.serena and never any live session's SERENA_HOME), instantiate a Serena agent in-process (no MCP server, no network port) against the already-indexed disposable-repo, then call RenameSymbolTool.apply on compute_total -> compute_grand_total and SafeDeleteSymbol.apply on report. Expect: (a) after rename, find_symbol for 'compute_total' returns no hits and for 'compute_grand_total' returns the function at its original location, with the call site inside Basket.total updated too; (b) after delete, find_symbol for 'report' returns no hits and the function body is removed from sample.py; (c) the real ~/.serena/ directory remains unchanged (still only memories/) throughout.
preregistration.criteria: settled for the Serena/Python arm if all three expectations hold; not_settled/deferred if the isolated run cannot be completed cleanly. jCodeMunch and codebase-memory-mcp arms are separately scoped (see below) and do not gate this criterion.

commands: rm -rf ~/.serena/language_servers ~/.serena/logs ~/.serena/prompt_templates ~/.serena/serena_config.yml (revert round-1 side effect; verified only memories/ remains)

tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/<live-serena-pid>/environ | grep SERENA_HOME (x2 pids) -> SERENA_HOME=/home/example/.local/share/codex-ecosystem/context/serena-home for every live session process, confirming ~/.serena/serena_config.yml is not read by any running instance

python3 script (run_serena_rename_test.py) executed with the venv's own interpreter (/home/example/.local/share/codex-ecosystem/context/serena-c6fbd1c/bin/python) and SERENA_HOME=/home/example/.cache/gap-wave2-20260923/code-navigation/serena-home-iso set in-process before importing serena: instantiates SerenaAgent(project=disposable-repo), gets RenameSymbolTool/SafeDeleteSymbol/FindSymbolTool, calls find_symbol before rename, rename_symbol, find_symbol for stale+fresh name after rename, reads the file, safe_delete_symbol on report, find_symbol for stale name after delete, reads the file again, then agent.reset()
ls -la ~/.serena/ before and after the script run -> unchanged (only memories/) both times
ps aux | grep -i 'gap-wave2\|serena-home-iso' after the script run -> no lingering process (agent.reset() tore down the per-project pyright language server it started)

results.shared_state_check: ls -la ~/.serena/ immediately before and immediately after the isolated run both show only the pre-existing memories/ directory; no serena_config.yml or other new file appeared under the real ~/.serena at any point in round 2.
results.jcodemunch_and_codebase_memory_mcp: Unchanged from round 1: no rename/delete/reindex action was identified in jCodeMunch's read-only, allow_state_change-gated action surface within the time-boxed scope of this check, and codebase-memory-mcp remains absent from this host (removed 2026-09-21, see gap-index-0 receipt). Neither was exercised for this gap in round 2 either.

limits: Settles the correctness assertion for exactly one tool (Serena) and one language (Python) in one disposable repo: rename correctly updates the definition and its in-file call site and removes all stale-name hits; delete correctly removes the symbol body and all hits. It does not settle the assertion for jCodeMunch (no identified rename/delete action) or codebase-memory-mcp (absent from host), so the full preregistered three-tool claim remains open.

The rename/delete test used Python's built-in AST-based rename path inside Serena rather than exercising a separate LSP-backed refactor for a second language; multi-language coverage (e.g. TypeScript, via the ts-lsp already running for live sessions) was not attempted within the time-box.

The test ran in-process (instantiating SerenaAgent directly and calling Tool.apply) rather than through the MCP transport a real client uses; this exercises the same underlying rename/delete/reindex code path Serena's MCP tools call, but does not additionally test the MCP request/response framing layer.

Round 1's false-hazard/incomplete-cleanup findings are corrected and remediated here: the four round-1-created paths under the real ~/.serena were deleted (backed up first to this unit's own cache directory), verified via before/after directory listings, and the corrected SERENA_HOME-based isolation approach was used and re-verified for round 2's own run (no new file appeared under the real ~/.serena at any point).
